code_quality.reasoning: The solution patch changes only `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js`, which is production code; it does not hand-edit generated/configuration files or introduce unrelated churn. The helpers are narrowly scoped, use the file's existing in-place request-normalization style, and the array path remains unchanged. The repository's ESLint configuration contains no visible rule violated by the new declarations or syntax. The ordering defect below is a completeness problem rather than an independent style, scope, or configured-gate problem.

issues.detail: Normalize/strip single-object message content before applying the spent-budget return, or otherwise make the 4-marker branch perform those required transformations. For example, a Claude native-passthrough request with one cache_control on system, one on a tool, one on an assistant array block, and one on `{ role: "user", content: { type: "text", text: "u", cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" } } }` has exactly four markers. The new `countCacheControlBlocks(body) >= 4` return leaves that user content as a bare object and leaves its cache_control intact. It therefore neither sends that turn as a one-element array nor removes its client marker. This is not repaired later: native Claude passthrough first calls `normalizeClaudePassthrough`, which preserves non-array content, then calls `anchorClaudeCache` immediately before execution.
issues.evidence: The description promises that a single-object turn is "delivered to the upstream API as a one-element array" and that "any cache_control marker the client placed on it is removed." `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:173-189` creates the native passthrough body and calls `normalizeClaudePassthrough`; `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js:160-163` and `240-241` preserve non-array non-system content; `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:299-302` calls `anchorClaudeCache` as the final cache step, and `chatCore.js:359` passes that same body to the executor.
issues.title: The 4-marker early return bypasses required single-object normalization and marker removal

evaluation.overall_feedback:
The solution patch is tightly scoped to one production translator file. Its `prepareClaudeRequest` changes correctly cover the normal translation path: a recognized bare block becomes an array before filtering, its marker is stripped in the existing block loop, and existing array-shaped turns take the same path they took before. The marker counter also covers the relevant system, tool, array-message, and bare-message locations, so the intended four-marker guard is clear.

The budget guard must not prevent the independent bare-content sanitation work. The native Claude path deliberately pins cache anchors after all other request processing, so a request exercising both reported defects reaches the new early return and is serialized upstream in the prohibited bare-object form with the prohibited client marker still present. Move the normalization and necessary bare-block marker cleanup ahead of the guard (and add a regression covering exactly four markers plus a bare block) so both guarantees hold together.

solution_comprehensiveness.reasoning: The preparation path is correctly addressed for ordinary translated requests: `prepareClaudeRequest` normalizes a bare content-block object before its cache-control removal and valid-content filtering, so supported text/tool/image/document blocks survive as one-element arrays with the client marker removed. Existing array content is a no-op through the new normalizer. `anchorClaudeCache` also counts markers across system, tools, and message content before it adds its normal anchors. However, its new budget guard returns before doing the newly added message normalization/marker cleanup, leaving a concrete combination of the two promised cases broken on the native Claude passthrough path.

evaluation.summary: The patch handles each defect in isolation but fails their valid four-marker/single-object intersection on the native Claude passthrough route.
